body.en: Evaluating, interpreting, and transforming functions runs through the Advanced Math domain: notation, shifts, composite functions, and piecewise branches.

blocks.heading: Level 1 · Foundations — Function Notation, Evaluation, Domain & Range

body.en: Master substituting numerical and algebraic inputs into function rules and determining valid domain constraints.

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Nonlinear Functions & Function Notation)

body.en:
Why Completing the Square & Log-Linearization Work: Any quadratic \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) (\(a \ne 0\)) can be rewritten by factoring \(a\) from the first two terms and adding/subtracting \((b/2a)^2\):

\[ ax^2 + bx + c = a\!\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 + \left(c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\right) \]

Because \(\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 \ge 0\) for all \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), the extreme value \(k = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\) is attained uniquely at the axis of symmetry \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), restricting the range to \([k, \infty)\) (if \(a > 0\)) and making \(f\) invertible on \(x \ge -\frac{b}{2a}\). Similarly, applying \(\ln\) to power laws \(y = ax^n\) yields \(\ln y = n\ln x + \ln a\), transforming a nonlinear curve into a straight line of gradient \(n\).

caption.en: Error Diagnosis — Common Student Traps vs. Exam-Board Method (Nonlinear Functions & Function Notation)

rows.en: Confuses the product law \(\ln(xy) = \ln x + \ln y\) with a non-existent sum rule.
Only factor products, quotients, and powers inside logarithms: \(\ln(xy) = \ln x + \ln y\).
Keeping both roots of \(\sqrt{2x+4} = x - 3\) without checking \(x - 3 \ge 0\)
Squaring both sides loses the sign of \(x - {r}\), introducing roots where \(\sqrt{\cdot} = -\text{number}\).
Enforce the range condition \(x \ge 3\) before or after squaring.
Restricting domain of \(f(x) = (x-3)^2 + 1\) to \(x \ge 0\) for invertibility
The vertex is at \(x = 3\), so \(f(2) = f(4) = 2\) fails the horizontal line test on \(x \ge 0\).
Restrict the domain at the vertex axis of symmetry: \(x \ge 3\) (or \(x \le 3\)).

label.en: ▲ Exam Pacing & Verification Strategy — Nonlinear Functions & Function Notation

body.en: Fast Exam Check (College Board Digital SAT Math): To verify an inverse function \(f^{-1}(x)\) in 5 seconds, pick a simple input \(x_0\), compute \(y_0 = f(x_0)\), and check that \(f^{-1}(y_0) = x_0\). Also verify that the graph of \(y = f^{-1}(x)\) reflects \(y = f(x)\) across \(y = x\).

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations

For the function \( f(x) = 2x^2 - 3x + 5 \), what is the value of \( f(-3) \)?

solution.en:
Substitute \( x = -3 \) into the expression, taking care with negative signs:

\[ f(-3) = 2(-3)^2 - 3(-3) + 5 = 2(9) + 9 + 5 = 18 + 9 + 5 = 32. \]

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in Nonlinear Functions & Function Notation and start from \( f(x) = 2x^2 - 3x + 5 \).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \( x = -3 \).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

blocks.heading: Level 2 · Medium — Graph Transformations & Composite Functions

body.en: Understand horizontal shifts \( f(x - h) \), vertical shifts \( f(x) + k \), reflections, and nested evaluations \( f(g(x)) \).

caption.en: The graph of \( g(x) = (x - 3)^2 + 2 \) is obtained by shifting the parent parabola \( f(x) = x^2 \) right by 3 units and up by 2 units, placing its vertex at \( (3, 2) \).

label.en: ⚠️ SAT Traps & Pitfalls — Function Transformations & Notation

body.en:
• Horizontal Shift Direction: \( f(x - c) \) shifts the graph \( c \) units to the right, whereas \( f(x + c) \) shifts it \( c \) units to the left.
  • Input vs. Output: For \( f(x) = 12 \), you are finding the input \( x \) that yields 12 (solving \( f(x) = 12 \)), NOT calculating \( f(12) \)!
  • Composition Evaluation Order: In \( f(g(x)) \), evaluate the innermost expression \( g(x) \) first, then pass the resulting value into \( f \).
  • Undefined Points / Domain Restrictions: Radical functions require non-negative radicands (\( x \ge 0 \)), and rational functions are undefined where the denominator is zero.

For \( f(x) = 3x - 5 \) and \( g(x) = x^2 + 2 \), evaluate \( g(f(2)) \).

Evaluate inner function: \( f(2) = 3(2) - 5 = 1 \).

Substitute into outer function: \( g(1) = 1^2 + 2 = 3 \).

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

Let \( f(x) = x - 4 \) and \( g(x) = 2x^2 + 1 \). If \( h(x) = g(f(x)) \), what is the value of \( h(1) \)?

solution.en:
Step 1: Evaluate inner function at 1: \[ f(1) = 1 - 4 = -3. \]

Step 2: Pass result into \( g(x) \): \[ g(-3) = 2(-3)^2 + 1 = 2(9) + 1 = 18 + 1 = 19. \]

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in Nonlinear Functions & Function Notation and start from \( f(x) = x - 4 \).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \( f(1) = 1 - 4 = -3. \).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

blocks.heading: Level 3 · Advanced — Piecewise Functions & Boundary Continuity

body.en: Evaluate piecewise-defined functions by identifying the active interval, and determine continuity at domain transitions.

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced

For the piecewise function \( g(x) = \begin{cases} 2x + 5 & x \le -1 \\ x^2 - 3 & x > -1 \end{cases} \), what is the value of \( g(-1) + g(3) \)?

solution.en:
Evaluate \( g(-1) \): Since \( -1 \le -1 \), use the first piece: \[ g(-1) = 2(-1) + 5 = 3. \]

Evaluate \( g(3) \): Since \( 3 > -1 \), use the second piece: \[ g(3) = 3^2 - 3 = 6. \]

Sum: \[ g(-1) + g(3) = 3 + 6 = 9. \]

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in Nonlinear Functions & Function Notation and write down the target quantity and domain conditions.
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \( g(-1) \).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

figure.title: Horizontal & Vertical Function Transformations: g(x) = f(x - 2) + 3

caption.en: Replacing x with (x - 2) shifts the graph 2 units right, while adding 3 outside the function shifts the graph 3 units up.

label.en: Level 4 (Synthesis) — Interpreting y-Intercept of Shifted Rational/Exponential Functions

body.en:
Problem: The function \( f(x) = 3^x + 4 \) is translated 2 units to the left and 5 units down to form \( g(x) \). What is the \( y \)-intercept of \( y = g(x) \)?

Solution: Translating 2 units left replaces \( x \) with \( x + 2 \), and 5 units down subtracts 5:

\[ g(x) = f(x + 2) - 5 = 3^{x+2} + 4 - 5 = 3^{x+2} - 1. \]

Evaluate at \( x = 0 \): \( g(0) = 3^2 - 1 = 8 \), so the \( y \)-intercept is \( (0, 8) \).

question.en:
Level 4 · Synthesis

If \( f(x - 3) = 4x + 5 \) for all real numbers \( x \), what is the value of \( f(2) \)?

solution.en:
To evaluate \( f(2) \), set the input expression \( x - 3 \) equal to \( 2 \):

\[ x - 3 = 2 \implies x = 5. \]

Substitute \( x = 5 \) into the right-hand side:

\[ f(2) = 4(5) + 5 = 25. \]

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in Nonlinear Functions & Function Notation and start from \( f(x - 3) = 4x + 5 \).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \( f(2) \).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.
